sections.title: Validating publish inputs
sections.key_moment: The site-name regex `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$` is a conservative-shell-safety hat. `site-builder` itself accepts almost anything, but the name flows through bash wrappers, CI logs, and (after linking) a SuiNS label — restricting it to filename-safe characters means no entry in the pipeline has to defend against quoting, control chars, or pathological lengths.

sections.title: Building the site-builder argv
sections.key_moment: `--context <network>` is a GLOBAL flag on `site-builder`, not a subcommand flag — it must precede `publish` in the argv. The function returns the argv as a string array (not a single shell-quoted string) so callers feed it to `execFile` / `spawn`, which sidesteps shell injection on the site name.

sections.title: Parsing site_object_id from stdout
sections.key_moment: `site-builder`'s stdout is a human-readable log; the line `site_object_id: 0x<hex>` is what we anchor on. Anchoring on the line shape (with the `m` regex flag) rather than greedy text matching keeps the parser tolerant to upstream log changes — a future CLI version can rearrange the surrounding text without breaking us as long as that one line shape survives.

sections.title: Building the SuiNS link Move call
sections.key_moment: The link is one Sui Move call to `<suins-pkg>::controller::set_target_walrus_site`, taking the NameRegistration object id and the site object id (in that order). Returning the payload as data — `{ target, args }` — instead of a built `Transaction` lets the test assert on PTB shape without pulling in `@mysten/sui`, and lets the caller pick either `Transaction.moveCall(...)` or `sui client call`.
